data.text:
Impact of a $15/bbl increase in oil prices on GDP of selected Asian countries.

I can say with confidence that the impact on the Philippines is grossly understated for the current situation.

That's because this crisis isn't just a matter of rising oil prices. It's also a matter of access to reliable and stable supplies.

As a nation that imports 90%+ of its oil and 2/3rds of its fuel, most coming from Middle East suppliers, the Philippines is extremely vulnerable to the production cuts now taking place in the region. Up to 50% lower output in some cases, which will eat away at exports to Asia.

The Philippines, being one of the smaller buyers, will not have priority to limited available supplies of oil and refined petroleum products. It will get some - but not all of what it requests.

If a global shortage takes form (as existing supplies run out), the GDP hit on the Philippines will be very noticeable. The streets are already experiencing thinning traffic, especially at night when trucks usually make deliveries. 

That's not just a sign of truck operators conserving on fuel. It's a big red light flashing that the economy is slowing down in a hurry.
